description: This Java source file defines the TenantActor class, which manages tenant-related actor behaviors in the Thingsboard platform, including initialization, message processing, and lifecycle management.

classes.name: TenantActor
classes.description: Main actor class managing tenant lifecycle, message processing, and interactions within the Thingsboard platform.

classes.name: TenantActor.ActorCreator
classes.description: Factory class for creating instances of TenantActor with specific tenant context.

methods.name: init
methods.description: Initializes the tenant actor, setting up tenant data, rule chains, and calculated field actors.

methods.name: destroy
methods.description: Cleans up resources and stops child actors when tenant actor is stopped.

methods.name: doProcess
methods.description: Processes incoming messages based on their type, handling tenant-specific logic.

methods.name: forwardToCfActor
methods.description: Forwards messages to the calculated field actor if initialized.

methods.name: isMyPartition
methods.description: Checks if an entity belongs to the current partition managed by this service.

methods.name: onQueueToRuleEngineMsg
methods.description: Handles messages directed to the rule engine, routing them appropriately.

methods.name: onToDeviceActorMsg
methods.description: Routes messages to device actors, considering priority and device deletion status.

methods.name: onPartitionChangeMsg
methods.description: Handles partition change events, initializing or stopping rule chains and actors accordingly.

methods.name: onComponentLifecycleMsg
methods.description: Handles lifecycle events of components, including API state updates and device deletions.

methods.name: getOrCreateDeviceActor
methods.description: Creates or retrieves a device actor for a specific device.

methods.name: getApiUsageState
methods.description: Retrieves the current API usage state, caching it for efficiency.

methods.name: onProcessFailure
methods.description: Handles failures during message processing, logging errors.
